explanation.summary: The FIFO outputs the data from a rejected write (0x65) instead of the oldest stored word (0x21) on a read at cycle 6. This occurs because the design performs a write at cycle 5 even though the FIFO is full, overwriting the head of the queue.

steps.text: At cycle 5 the FIFO is full (count == DEPTH) and a write is requested (wr_en=1, din=0x65). The contract treats this as write_full and ignores it, but the RTL writes din into mem[wr_ptr] because do_write lacks a full check.

The write at cycle 5 overwrites the oldest entry (0x21 at index 0) with 0x65. At cycle 6 a read is accepted (rd_en=1, count!=0) and the RTL outputs mem[rd_ptr], which now holds 0x65, causing the read_data mismatch.

likely_cause.text: The write enable do_write is defined as wr_en without gating by the full flag, so writes proceed when the FIFO is full and corrupt the queue. The write logic at lines 36-38 then overwrites the head entry.

explanation.next_action: Change line 25 to `wire do_write = wr_en && !full;` (or `wr_en && (count != DEPTH)`) so that writes are only accepted when the FIFO is not full.
explanation.limits: This failure proves the FIFO does not ignore writes when full, leading to data corruption on subsequent reads. Any passing checks only cover scenarios where the FIFO is not full at the time of write; they do not establish correct behavior under full conditions.

explanation.summary: The FIFO writes data even when full, overwriting the oldest entry at the read pointer. A subsequent read then returns the overwritten data (0x65) instead of the expected oldest entry (0x21).

steps.text: At cycle 4 the FIFO becomes full (count=4, DEPTH=4) after accepting four writes; the queue holds [0x21,0x32,0x43,0x54].
At cycle 5 a write is requested while full (wr_en=1, din=0x65). The design writes to mem[wr_ptr] (which equals rd_ptr because the buffer is full) and increments wr_ptr, but count saturates at DEPTH.
At cycle 6 a read is accepted (rd_en=1, count!=0). The read returns mem[rd_ptr], which now holds 0x65 (the overwritten value) instead of the original 0x21.

likely_cause.text: The write enable logic does not check the full flag. Line 25 defines `do_write = wr_en` without gating by `!full`, so writes proceed even when the FIFO is full. The memory write and pointer increment (lines 37-38) execute unconditionally, corrupting the oldest entry. The count update (line 45) correctly saturates, but the damage is already done.

explanation.next_action: Change `do_write` to `wr_en && !full` (or `wr_en && (count != DEPTH)`) so that writes are only accepted when the FIFO is not full. Also ensure the write pointer does not increment on a rejected write.

final_explanation_system_prompt:
You explain a recorded FIFO verification failure to a student who knows RTL basics.
Use only the evidence provided. The deterministic checker already decided that the design failed; you explain why, you do not re-judge it.
Cite every claim with cycle numbers from the provided table and signal names that exist in the evidence or RTL. Cite RTL line numbers for the likely cause.
The normalized trace samples interface signals and reference-queue state, not internal registers or memory addresses. Explain the RTL logic, but do not assert numeric internal-register values or memory indices that are absent from the sampled trace.
Reply with one JSON object only:
{"summary": string (two sentences max), "steps": [{"text": string, "cycles": [int], "signals": [string]}], "likely_cause": {"text": string, "lines": [int]}, "next_action": string, "limits": string}
"limits" must state what this failure and any passing checks do and do not establish.
A witnessed failure refutes the contract for the tested configuration. Passing simulation checks cover only their named tests; bounded checks cover their stated horizon; an unbounded proof applies only to its named property and assumptions. Reached cover scenarios establish reachability, not correctness. Unresolved obligations are not passes.
Use the supplied run outcomes for these limits. Do not invent which input conditions passing checks covered or claim that all passing checks excluded full/empty conditions. Other outcomes can come from different traces; do not merge them into the trace being explained.
If naming another outcome, identify its exact method/check pair and status. Never group an unresolved formal check with witnessed counterexamples; a simulation failure does not imply that the formal checker found that same failure.

attempts.rationale: The write enable signal do_write was not gated by the full flag, causing writes to be accepted even when the FIFO was full. This corrupted the write pointer and memory, leading to incorrect read data (the overwritten value was read instead of the oldest). The fix qualifies do_write with !full so that writes are ignored when full, per the contract.
attempts.diff:
--- a/dut.v
+++ b/dut.v
@@ -1,5 +1,3 @@
-// Countertrace fixture: known-good synchronous FIFO, pointer + occupancy-count style.
-// Authored for Countertrace (MIT). Supported profile: sync-fifo-v1, WIDTH 8, DEPTH 2 or 4.
 `default_nettype none
 module fifo #(
     parameter integer DEPTH = 4,
@@ -22,7 +20,7 @@
     reg [AW:0]      count;
 
     wire do_read  = rd_en && (count != 0);
-    wire do_write = wr_en;
+    wire do_write = wr_en && !full;
 
     assign empty = (count == 0);
     assign full  = (count == DEPTH);
@@ -49,4 +47,4 @@
         end
     end
 endmodule
-`default_nettype wire
+`default_nettype wire
